scopes.headline: Layer 1 (web tokens and themes): 1 of 9 subjects ready (Figma sync model); 0 P0, 3 P1, 15 P2, 9 P3. The biggest problem: brand and surface axes do not work in nested scopes. The semantic tokens derived from them are declared only on the mode scope, so UIProvider brand= or surface= without mode changes the primary fill but not links, focus ring or surfaces. Second: the reverse shadcn bridge leaves 139 recipe tokens undefined. Other gaps: radius and type scale work only at the root, the type ramp has 1px steps and line heights that go down, chart-2 and chart-3 are about 2:1 on the light page, there are about 59 dead tokens the economy check cannot see, Tailwind has no danger status roles, there is no procedure for adding a theme, and Figma shows defaults for about 15 terminal/retro material tokens. The styles browser tests were not run this round; CI passed on 77fd109 with identical packages/styles.

最大问题是命名不一致和 iOS 映射缺口：contract 层还没 ready（78 个评分对象里只有 7 个 ready，都是 preview 组件），共 3 个 P1。第一，39 条一致性债务仍在 baseline 里，consumer 能直接碰到，比如 ButtonGroup/Tabs 用 size="default"，Button 用 size="md"；lint 还漏掉 aligns/alignments、sides/directions、on/selected/checked、accent/primary 这类近义名。第二，31 个有 iOS 对应物的 contract 里，有 17 个没有任何轴映射，generator 也不拦。第三，69 个组件标了 stable，但还没有一张评分卡是 ready 的（这条要 YZ 拍板）。P2 有 11 条：13 个 contract 的 states 漏了 recipe 实际画出的状态（starting/ending、focus-visible、hover）；6 个轴没有默认值；menu 是共享 recipe，却被登记成 stable 组件，CLI 也查不到它；另外还有 Button、Input、Toaster、Toggle Group 的映射缺口。生成的 contract 文件和 CI 接线是好的（check:contracts 两个脚本 rc=0）。K10 不在 contract 层，没有评分。

最大问题是 Y1 证据缺口：24 个对象没有一个 ready。除 list-page 外，所有模板和区块都只在 390 和 1280 两个宽度有基线截图；AppView 自己的 phone 故事是按 1280 宽截的；Page 和 Section 没有任何故事。共 2 个 P1：一是 `atom63 copy dashboard-page` 漏掉了 list-page-data.ts，复制出来的页面编译不过；二是没有任何入口能把 builder 带到 ReaderLayout。另有 16 个 P2，涉及 safe-area 漏洞（AppView 在 inset 加 topBarSpan=main 时、app-view 手机示例直接写 env()）、stat-row 长数值会溢出、平板宽度下隐藏了 Amount 列、缺少压力测试故事，以及 tab-bar 写死的 11px 字号。

The biggest problem is that npm `latest` is stale on all 8 published packages. The trusted publisher gets a 403 when it tries to move dist-tags, so a plain `npm install @atom63/ui-react` gets beta.9 from September, even though the README says it gets the current beta. The second P1 is that mdx labels 13 of its entries 'stable' while still at 0.4.0-beta. No subject is ready: A5 scores 1 on every package. Dependency direction is one-way with no cycles, but no check enforces it. The ui-react bundle budget is a ratchet at 99.4 of 100 kB. 37 public types in mdx, widgets and ui-react cannot be imported by name. The webkit sign-in flake still fails CI.

None of the 5 layer-6 subjects is ready. Two P1s: 7 of 15 AGENTS.md rules have no check and no reason why not, and the case-study outcome can't be shown on this main (the Round 13 reports aren't committed, no rerun since, failures not traced to a layer). P2s: a misspelled token gets unrelated results, the starter still gives agents only the docs (no CLI or MCP), @atom63/create is unpublished, npm latest tags point at older betas, 223 of 778 exports are named in no docs, and the CRM vibe run (Atom63 arms 17-20 points below plain) was never rerun. The CLI and MCP agree with each other and with the contracts (MCP test 17/17 pass, 76/76 component statuses match).

None of the 8 batch-1 action components is ready. There are no P0 or P1 findings, but every subject has at least one criterion at 2 (23 P2s, 12 P3s). The biggest problem is grouped buttons: they clip Button's 44px touch target, so cells are 32px on touch, and a pressed member cannot be told apart in forced-colors mode. Button also has two gaps: loading drops keyboard focus, and render keeps the native disabled attribute and type=button on a non-button element. Other gaps repeat across the batch: CopyButton and DestinationLink hardcode English text, ToggleGroup's size and tone props are missing from its contract, and PanelSettingButton can only be used controlled. Visual quality (K3) is scored provisionally and waits for YZ: Toggle is flat in aqua and retro, DestinationLink looks the same in every theme, and the active PanelSettingButton icon looks dim in dark modes. The CLI pages for the smaller components are boilerplate with no code example, and CopyButton's size table is wrong. Hover and focus-visible states have no baselines anywhere in the batch.

The biggest problem is that SegmentedControl's selected segment disappears under forced colors (P1). Only checkbox, radio and switch are ready (3 of 8). Segmented-control, slider, rating, progress and spinner are blocked by 15 P2 findings: the slider rail measures 1.02-1.18:1 and vanishes under forced colors; rating stars measure 2.04:1 and 1.64:1 in light mode and the input rating is controlled-only; the Slider and Progress default tone of accent conflicts with AGENTS.md rule 5 (needs a YZ decision); spinner has no props type, injects a style element into every instance, hard-codes an English label and its CLI example does not run in a consumer app. K10 is n/a (iOS backlog). K3 taste scores are provisional until YZ sees the contact sheets.

最大问题是表单字段的交互状态和触屏尺寸没有证据：本批 10 个组件只有 label 和 amount 达到 ready，另外 8 个都卡在 P2，没有 P0/P1。(1) 没有任何字段组件有 hover 或 focus-visible 的截图基线（visual/commands.ts 会把指针挪开，story 里也没有 play()），input-themes 里叫 "focused-look" 的那一行其实画的是 invalid 状态。(2) 不是 phone form factor 时，粗指针下 Input、SearchField、OTP、Select、Autocomplete 的输入框和选项都只有 32px 高（environment.css:128-137），达不到 44px。(3) 各组件 API 不一致：Autocomplete 的尺寸写成 sm/default/lg，className 加在 input 上而不是外层 group，它的 Popup 也不读 PortalContainerProvider（autocomplete.tsx:59,107,160）。Field 的 invalid/disabled 没有对应的 prop，只能手写 data-invalid="true"，而且渲染 FieldError 时 label 不会变红。SearchField 的 contract 写了 search-field-input 这个 slot，代码里从来没渲染。InputOTP 没有 invalid prop，也没导出类型。Input 和 Textarea 用 unstyled、shadow 两个布尔 prop 充当变体。(4) 无障碍：Autocomplete 没有绑定 APG 模式，也没有键盘测试；Select 有 5 处已记录的 APG 偏差；FormControl 的 aria-describedby 总是指向 description id，没渲染 FormDescription 时也一样，FormMessage 同时写了 role=alert 和 aria-live=polite（form.tsx:113,146,150）。(5) SearchField 没有 Themes story，query 状态也没有截图基线。K3 是暂定分，要 YZ 看过截图对照表才算数；K10 记为 n/a: iOS backlog。

Biggest problem: PortalContainer's promise is broken. Dialog, AlertDialog and Drawer, plus Command, ContextMenu, NavigationMenu and Autocomplete, ignore the provider (P1). None of the 10 overlays is ready. The 36 P2s cluster in five places. (1) Sheet, Drawer, Popover, HoverCard and PreviewCard have no APG binding or keyboard tests, and Sheet and Drawer have no aria-modal. (2) Several visual baselines can't be judged: the Drawer captures are closed, the Popover and PreviewCard theme captures overlap, Tooltip shows only 1 of 8 combos, and the Toaster Playground has no toast. (3) Side sheets and drawers skip the top and bottom safe areas, and Popover and PreviewCard have no max-height. (4) HoverCard and PreviewCard wrap the same primitive and colliding aliases are exported (YZ decides which stays). (5) API leftovers: Dialog's scrollFade does nothing, PopoverAnchor does nothing, AlertDialog's API drifts from Dialog's, and the Dialog close button is 32px on coarse pointers. K10 is n/a (iOS backlog); K3 scores are provisional until YZ checks.

None of the 9 batch-5 menu and navigation subjects is ready. There are 6 P1s: two focus or highlight states vanish under forced colors (NavigationMenu links have no focus ring at all; Command's highlighted row is a fill with no forced-colors rule), the menu contract has no CLI answer, and ContextMenu, Menubar and NavigationMenu have no behaviour tests. The common P2s are menu, command and nav rows only 32px tall on touch, open states missing from the visual baselines, unmirrored chevrons in RTL and English labels that callers cannot replace. Tabs is closest to ready: its only gap is touch height, a declared exception that YZ needs to rule on.

Batch 6 (surfaces and structure): 1 of 10 ready (frame). The biggest problem is that a vertical Separator renders invisible in auto-height rows; its Themes baseline is blank and still passes (P1, needs verifiedBy). The 36 P2s cluster in four areas: contract and prop drift (scroll-area has an orientation axis but no prop; connected-panel has an undeclared variant; scrollable-list and separator props differ from their contract axes); contract states with no stories (disabled is uncaptured in accordion, collapsible, resizable, scrollable-list and connected-panel); no forced-colors handling (separator, item selection, resizable, scroll-area thumb); and specific bugs (Accordion className replaces its base class, collapsible prop is a no-op, Item line-clamps never apply, ConnectedPanel aria-controls points at unmounted content). K10 is n/a (iOS backlog).

最大问题是批次 7 没有一个组件达到 ready：8 个里 0 个就绪，4 个 P1。问题是：sidebar 折叠成图标栏后按钮没有可访问名称；sidebar 在 RTL 下 menu action 和 badge 盖住标签开头；sidebar-nav-tree 的 Themes 基线图坏了，8 个主题/模式组合只拍到 1 个；marquee 默认参数下会一直滚动、没有暂停办法，不符合 WCAG 2.2.2。31 个 P2 集中在几类：forced-colors 下选中态全靠背景色（sidebar、table、calendar、carousel 的 dots），硬编码英文文案，carousel 和 text-ticker 会覆盖调用方传入的 ref，calendar、marquee、text-ticker 的 CLI 指引是套话，以及触屏目标偏小（sidebar 32px，calendar 36px）。K10 全部按要求记为 n/a（iOS backlog）。只写了这一个输出文件，没有改源码和 git 状态。

Batch 8 (feedback and status): only Badge is ready, 1 of 8. The biggest problem is accessibility. I measured from the baselines and three status texts fail contrast that axe did not flag: Alert's success and warning action labels at 3.58:1 and 3.28:1, and Empty's 'Show details' toggle at 2.51:1. FeedbackState's loading live region uses aria-busy and then drops its role, so neither loading nor the result gets announced. FeedbackState also spreads no props and forwards no ref, and LoadMoreTrigger's Retry button is about 15px tall with no touch target. That makes 5 P1s, 17 P2s, 7 P3s and no P0. The P2s include physical positioning that check:craft does not catch (Avatar badge, Empty copy button), Skeleton's shimmer always sweeping left to right, which ignores the contract's leading-to-trailing direction, an Avatar group count that ignores the xs size, and no example of the IntersectionObserver wiring LoadMoreTrigger needs. K10 is n/a for every subject (iOS backlog). Taste scores (K3) are provisional until YZ confirms them.

Batch 9 (chat): 0 of 5 subjects are ready. The biggest problem is the one P1: ChatTypingIndicator's screen-reader announcement is unreliable. It is a role=status with only an aria-label, and every documented placement puts it inside an aria-busy ChatMessage. Its dots also disappear under forced colors. The 8 P2s: the composer strands focus on a disabled send button after a send and has no phone story. ChatMessage and Message bubbles have no forced-colors treatment, and Message's bubble clips focus outlines. ChatMessage has no error state. Message's delivered and read look the same, and its Themes baseline skips ThemeMatrix, so retro and terminal show modern rounded bubbles. The ChatSteps trigger is 32px on touch. K10 is n/a (iOS backlog).

The biggest problem is that none of the 48 package subjects is ready. K3 tops out at 2 everywhere because no package surface has theme captures (0 aqua/retro/terminal baselines, 16 of 205 dark), and no SSR smoke test covers mdx/inform/widgets/brand stories. There are 3 P1s: VideoBlock can autoplay and loop forever with no pause control and ignores reduced motion (WCAG 2.2.2). Widget controls stay at 24px on touch because the 44px --widget-interaction-target is defined but nothing uses it. And 26 MDX blocks have no props, examples or a CLI answer. The 25 P2s add width-based instead of pointer-based targets in mdx and a 24px inform dismiss target. Inform also lacks forced-colors, safe-area and logical placement support. Blocks drop id/aria props, and English strings and physical insets are hard-coded where check:craft misses them. K10 is n/a (iOS backlog).

findings.subject: workspace: release pipeline and CI
findings.summary: npm `latest` is stale on all 8 published packages (ui-react latest 0.2.0-beta.9 from 2026-09-24 vs beta 0.2.0-beta.12) because the trusted publisher cannot move dist-tags; the publish job fails after publishing, so tags and registry evidence are skipped too, and README.md tells consumers a plain install gets the beta.
findings.evidence: Release beta run 44371320697: 'npm error 403 403 Forbidden - PUT .../@atom63%2fstyles/dist-tags/latest - This trusted publisher cannot manage dist-tags'. npm view @atom63/<pkg> dist-tags (2026-11-19): styles latest 0.1.0-beta.5 / beta 0.1.0-beta.8; ui-foundation 0.1.1-beta.2 / 0.2.0-beta.5; ui-react 0.2.0-beta.9 / 0.2.0-beta.12; mdx 0.4.0-beta.0 / 0.4.0-beta.3; inform 0.2.0-beta.0 / 0.2.0-beta.3; agent 0.3.0-beta.0 / 0.3.0-beta.1; widgets 0.1.0-beta.0 / 0.1.0-beta.3; cli 0.1.0-beta.0 / 0.1.0-beta.1. README.md:15-17 claims latest follows beta; release-automation.md:42 says 'Allow npm dist-tag' must be enabled. No git tag for ui-react@0.2.0-beta.12 (git ls-remote --tags). Untagged installs documented in packages/inform/README.md:6, packages/widgets/README.md:7, packages/agent/README.md:7, packages/ui-foundation/README.md:23.
findings.fix: Enable 'Allow npm dist-tag' on each package's trusted publisher (YZ/maintainer on npmjs.com), rerun the dist-tag step (or `npm dist-tag add <pkg>@<beta> latest` once), then add a CI/registry-smoke assertion that latest == beta for every published package and run check:stable-release-preflight in CI over all 8 packages.

verified.reason: Reproduced. `npm view` shows `latest` behind `beta` on all 8 packages, exactly as stated (for example ui-react latest 0.2.0-beta.9, beta 0.2.0-beta.12). The failed-job log of run 44371320697 shows `PUT .../@atom63%2fstyles/dist-tags/latest` returning 403 with "This trusted publisher cannot manage dist-tags". In that run Publish beta = failure and Record registry smoke evidence = skipped. `git ls-remote --tags origin` has no ui-react@0.2.0-beta.12, styles@0.1.0-beta.8 or mdx@0.4.0-beta.3 tag (ui-react stops at beta.11). README.md:15-17 still says a plain install gets the beta, and stable-release-policy.json sets latest.followsBetaBeforeStable:true. packages/{agent,ui-foundation,widgets,inform}/README.md tell readers to use an untagged `pnpm add`, which installs the stale `latest`. The fix is to enable 'Allow npm dist-tag' in npm settings (release-automation.md:42), but until then the A5 dist-tag and registry evidence is broken and the docs are wrong. P1 holds. Note: the later Release beta runs (2026-11-19/20) succeed only because nothing new was published.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: One concept still has several names across contracts: 39 known drift entries remain in the baseline (8 sizes `default` instead of `md`, 19 state synonyms, 8 physical left/right, 2 camelCase `focusVisible`, 1 `destructive` vs `error`), and a consumer hits them directly: `size="md"` type-checks on Button, Input, Select, Textarea and Segmented Control but not on Tabs, Dialog, Alert Dialog, Avatar, Item, Table, Autocomplete or Button Group.
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/contract-consistency-baseline.json (39 keys, e.g. "synonym | tabs.sizes | default -> md", "synonym | button-group.sizes | default -> md", "physical-value | sheet.sides | left"); packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/tabs.json:8 sizes ["xs","sm","default","lg"] vs button.json sizes [..."md"...]; `pnpm -s atom63 component tabs` prints "| `sizes` | `xs`, `sm`, `default`, `lg` | `default` |". check:contract-consistency passes only because these are baselined (sweep-r1/contract-consistency.log: "Contract consistency OK (77 contracts)").
findings.fix: Rename to the canonical values the lint already names (sizes default->md, states focus/idle/resting/default/active/hovering -> focus-visible/rest/current/hover, left/right -> start/end, focusVisible -> focus-visible, alert-dialog destructive -> error), keeping the old values as deprecated aliases (as button.json intent.stateAliases does) until a breaking release, then shrink the baseline with `pnpm check:contract-consistency --write`.

verified.reason: Reproduced: docs/design-system/audits/contract-consistency-baseline.json holds exactly 39 keys (8 `default -> md` sizes, 19 state synonyms, 8 physical left/right, 2 `focusVisible`, 1 `destructive -> error`). Size lists in packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components: button/input/select/textarea/segmented-control use `md`; tabs, dialog, alert-dialog, avatar, item, table, autocomplete and button-group use `default`. packages/ui-react/src/components/tabs/tabs.tsx:26 takes `size?: TabsSize` with `size = tabsContract.defaultSize`, so `size="md"` does not type-check there. `pnpm -s atom63 component tabs` prints sizes `xs, sm, default, lg`. The lint passes only because these entries are baselined. Consumers see this directly, so it blocks C2.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: 17 of the 31 contracts with a SwiftUI renderer have web axes but no `intent` block, so none of their axes are mapped to iOS (dialog, alert-dialog, field, textarea, switch, select, toggle, segmented-control, radio, slider, dropdown-menu, accordion, calendar, tabs, empty, load-more-trigger, destination-link); the 12 that do have one mostly map a single axis. Nothing fails on it: intentProblems returns [] when there is no intent.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-foundation/contracts/cross-renderer.json (31 components); node survey of contracts/components/*.json: intent present on button, input, toggle-group, card, badge, avatar, alert, progress, toaster, item, carousel, message only; scripts/design-system/lib/component-contracts.mjs:234-235 "const intent = source.doc.intent / if (!intent) return []"; e.g. tabs.json has variants/sizes/orientations and crossRenderer.swiftUIRenderer "Picker(.segmented) / AtomTabRow" with no mapping; toggle.json sizes+tones -> "AtomChip" unmapped; avatar intent maps only `ring` (sizes, shapes unmapped); item intent maps only `surface`. docs/design-system/cross-renderer-contracts.md:46 still says only Button, Badge and Input have intent.
findings.fix: Require an `intent` block for every component in cross-renderer.json and, in intentProblems, require every web axis list (variants, sizes, tones, orientations, ...) to be either mapped on both platforms or declared a web extension with a reason; then author the missing mappings, starting with the 17 that have none.

verified.reason: Reproduced: cross-renderer.json lists 31 components. `intent` appears only on alert, avatar, badge, button, card, carousel, input, item, message, progress, toaster and toggle-group (12), and toggle, select, tabs etc. have `intent: null`. component-contracts.mjs:235 has `if (!intent) return []`. avatar maps only `ring` and item only `surface`. cross-renderer-contracts.md:46 still says 'Button, Badge and Input also declare an intent block'. This is the round-0 contracts-3 gap, only partly closed.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Under forced colors the selected segment is indistinguishable: selection is drawn only by the indicator fill, its shadow and a text-colour change, all of which forced colors replace.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/segmented-control/segmented-control.css has no @media (forced-colors) block; selection = indicator background/box-shadow (lines 164-185) + item colour (100-102, 198-200). packages/ui-react/src/styles/recipes.test.ts:363-378 documents that 'a state drawn by colour alone vanishes' and guards tabs and toggle-group, not segmented-control.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors block: `.a63-SegmentedControl-indicator { background-color: Highlight; forced-color-adjust: none }` and `.a63-SegmentedControl-item[data-active] { color: HighlightText; forced-color-adjust: none }`; add 'segmented-control' to the it.each list in recipes.test.ts and a ForcedColors story/baseline like radio's.

verified.reason: segmented-control.css has no forced-colors block (grep finds none). Selection is drawn only by the indicator's background-color/box-shadow (indicator rule ~lines 164-185) and the [data-active] item colour. Forced colors replace both fills with Canvas, drop box-shadow and force the text to CanvasText, so the selected segment cannot be told apart. The focus outline appears only on :focus-visible. recipes.test.ts lines 363-378 guard tabs and toggle-group but not segmented-control, which is the same class of gap as the round-0 radio P1.

findings.subject: portal-container
findings.summary: PortalContainerProvider is ignored by Dialog, AlertDialog and Drawer (and Command, ContextMenu, NavigationMenu, Autocomplete), although its docs and CLI answer say package overlays render into it.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.tsx:48, alert-dialog/alert-dialog.tsx:30, drawer/drawer.tsx:124 render Base UI Portal without container; grep usePortalContainer lists only dropdown-menu, hover-card, popover, preview-card, select, sheet, toaster, tooltip; portal-container.tsx:5-8 and `atom63 component portal-container` claim otherwise. In a shadow root or nested theme region a Dialog escapes to document.body and loses its tokens/styles.
findings.fix: Make every portalling part fall back to usePortalContainer() as SheetPortal does (sheet.tsx:79-89), and add one test per overlay (or a shared table test) that it portals into the provider.

verified.reason: Reproduced from source. Only toaster, tooltip, preview-card, hover-card, dropdown-menu, popover, select, sheet and media-lightbox call usePortalContainer (grep). dialog.tsx:48-49, alert-dialog.tsx:30-31, drawer.tsx:124-125, context-menu.tsx:77-78 and autocomplete.tsx:160 render a Base UI Portal without a context container. command.tsx:72 uses a bare CommandDialogPortal, and navigation-menu.tsx:120 takes only an explicit portalContainer prop. portal-container.tsx:5-8 says the context carries the node that 'popovers, tooltips, dialogs' render into. `node packages/cli/src/bin.mjs component portal-container` says it 'supplies a shared mount target to package overlays' and lists Dialog as related. Callers can work around it with portalProps.container, so it is a documented-behaviour gap (P1), not a P0 break.

findings.subject: navigation-menu
findings.summary: NavigationMenuLink has no focus ring: `outline: none` with only a muted background on :focus-visible, which disappears under forced colors; the current link shares the same fill as hover/focus.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.css:204-231 (outline: none at :217; :focus-visible,[data-active] { background: var(--a63-surface-muted) } at :223-226); no forced-colors block in the file; styles/reset.css has no focus-visible fallback; AGENTS.md rule 12.
findings.fix: Give .a63-NavigationMenu-link:focus-visible the control focus-ring outline with a negative offset (as the trigger does at :90-94); draw [data-active] with a distinct marker (weight or an inline-start/underline bar) separate from hover; add a forced-colors block (focus outline in Highlight, active link in Highlight/HighlightText) and add navigation-menu to recipes.test.ts forced-colors list.

verified.reason: navigation-menu.css:217 sets outline:none on .a63-NavigationMenu-link and :223-226 gives :focus-visible and [data-active] the same surface-muted background, which hover also uses (:227-231). The file has no forced-colors block, so under forced colors the focused link has no indicator. This also breaks AGENTS.md rule 12 (focus rings must be outlines).

findings.subject: command
findings.summary: Command's highlighted option is drawn by background only with outline none and no forced-colors rule, so under forced colors the option Enter will run is invisible; CommandInput also always autoFocuses.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/command/command.css:174-200 (outline: none at :193, highlight via background-color at :195-200), no @media (forced-colors) in command.css; command absent from packages/ui-react/src/styles/recipes.test.ts:368-377; command.tsx:144 `autoFocus` hard-coded; CommandDialogPopup unnamed in command.stories.tsx:159,192.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors block repainting .a63-Command-item[data-highlighted] in Highlight/HighlightText (mirror menu.css:221-236) and add 'command' to the recipes forced-colors test; make autoFocus opt-in (default only inside CommandDialogPopup); document/require an aria-label or title on CommandDialogPopup and set one in the Dialog story.

verified.reason: command.css:193 sets outline:none and :195-200 draws [data-highlighted] with background, gloss and shadow only. command.css has no forced-colors rule, and command is missing from the forced-colors list in recipes.test.ts:368-377. Focus stays in the input (combobox), so under forced colors the active option is invisible. The autoFocus sub-point is weak: command.tsx:144 spreads {...props} after autoFocus, so a caller can override it.

findings.subject: navigation-menu
findings.summary: NavigationMenu has no behaviour tests: no open/close, hover, Escape, arrow-key or link-activation coverage and no open-state baseline.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.test.tsx:31-54 (3 render tests; `grep -c 'userEvent|fireEvent'` = 0); not bound in apps/storybook/a11y/patterns.test.ts:55-100; baselines ui-react-navigationmenu-*.png all closed.
findings.fix: Add userEvent tests for trigger click/hover open, Escape closing with focus return, ArrowLeft/Right between triggers, Tab into content, Link active -> aria-current; add an open-panel story (defaultValue) to the visual baselines.

verified.reason: navigation-menu.test.tsx has 3 tests (lines 31, 44, 54), all render or helper checks, with 0 userEvent/fireEvent/click/keyboard calls. patterns.test.ts bindings (lines 57-100) include only dialog, alertDialog, dropdownMenu, tabs, select, switch, checkbox, accordion and radio. Under K9 that leaves behaviour untested.

findings.subject: menubar

findings.subject: separator
findings.summary: A vertical Separator collapses to zero height in any flex row whose height is not fixed, so it is invisible in the Themes contact sheet for all 8 theme x mode combinations.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/separator/separator.css:18-22 (height:100% plus align-self:stretch; the percentage is indefinite and prevents stretch); apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-separator-themes-chromium-linux.png shows Home / Docs / About with no dividers, while ui-react-separator-vertical-chromium-linux.png shows them only because separator.stories.tsx:38 fixes the parent height to 24px.
findings.fix: Drop height:100% for vertical (leave height auto so align-self:stretch fills the row, with a min-block-size such as 1em as a floor), add a test that a vertical separator in an align-items:center row has a non-zero height, and re-baseline Themes.

verified.reason: separator.css:18-22 gives the vertical separator height:100% as well as align-self:stretch. Flexbox only stretches an item whose cross size computes to auto, and 100% is not auto, so stretch is ignored. The percentage then resolves against a parent row with no set height, so it acts as auto, and an empty element gets 0px. I reproduced this from the source: the Themes story (separator.stories.tsx:76-95, a flex row with no height) shows no dividers in any of the 8 theme x mode rows of ui-react-separator-themes-chromium-linux.png. The Vertical story renders them only because its row sets height:24 (stories:38). ButtonGroup, ToggleGroup and similar components draw their own separators in their own CSS, so the bug hits the standalone Separator in its usual inline-row use. That is broken output that blocks ready, so P1 stands.

findings.subject: marquee
findings.summary: With its default props the marquee moves forever with no way to pause it, failing WCAG 2.2.2 (level A).

findings.fix: Pause on hover and focus-within by default (make pauseOnHover default true, or always pause on focus-within), and document or offer a pause control for strips that run longer than 5 seconds; test it.

verified.reason: marquee.tsx:27-28 defaults pauseOnHover and paused to false. marquee.css:39 runs an infinite linear animation. The hover and focus-within pause rules (css:52-55) apply only with data-pause-on-hover. Only prefers-reduced-motion stops the motion (css:75-85, plus the scroll region at tsx:40-43). The component ships no pause control, and its contract and docs give no guidance on WCAG 2.2.2. So a default <Marquee> moves indefinitely next to other content and the user cannot pause it.

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Alert success and warning action labels fail text contrast (3.58:1 and 3.28:1), and every Alert is an assertive role=alert with no announced tone.
findings.evidence: Measured from apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-alert-action-variants-chromium-linux.png (darkest glyph vs fill): success 3.58:1, warning 3.28:1, need 4.5:1. alert.css:164 and :179 set --alert-action-foreground to --a63-status-success / --a63-status-warning; alert.tsx:26 hard-codes role="alert"; tone only in data-variant.
findings.fix: Use text-role tokens for the action foreground (as error does with --a63-text-danger; add --a63-text-success/-warning if missing) and declare those pairs in the contrast test. Default role to status (or none) for persistent alerts with role="alert" opt-in, and add a visually hidden tone prefix so the tone is announced.

verified.reason: alert.css:164 and :179 set --alert-action-foreground to --a63-status-success / --a63-status-warning, which are color-success-600 rgb(0,147,88) and color-warning-600 rgb(194,117,0) (primitives.css:261,272). Computed against the 4% tinted fill, that gives 3.77:1 and 3.43:1, short of the 4.5:1 needed for action label text. semantics.css:229-230 says these status tokens are tuned for 3:1 graphics, and text is meant to use the *-subtle-foreground steps (error already uses --a63-text-danger at :134). The role part is weaker than reported: alert.tsx:26 does hard-code role=alert, but {...props} comes after it, so a consumer can override it. That half is a P2 default-semantics gap. The contrast failure alone holds P1.

findings.subject: empty
findings.summary: Empty's 'Show details' toggle text is about 2.5:1 against the surface.

That is 2.51:1, computed again here. The text is 12px (control-font-size-xs) at rest, and only :hover restores full secondary colour (empty.css:119-121). This is a WCAG 1.4.3 failure on an interactive label.

findings.subject: feedback-state
findings.summary: FeedbackState's loading live region is aria-busy, and the result states drop the live region, so loading and its outcome go unannounced; the title is not a heading.
findings.evidence: feedback-state.tsx:174-180: aria-busy=true on the role=status region while loading; role/aria-live become undefined for empty, no-results, not-found, offline and stale. Title is a plain div (lines 189-191) while EmptyTitle is role=heading (empty.tsx:53-58). The test at feedback-state.test.tsx:23-32 asserts this pattern.
findings.fix: Keep one persistent polite status region that always exists, drop aria-busy from it (put aria-busy on the content region the consumer is loading if anything), keep role=alert only for error, and render the title as a heading (configurable level).

verified.reason: feedback-state.tsx:174-180 puts aria-busy=true on the role=status/aria-live=polite region while loading. Busy regions have their announcements suppressed, so 'Loading…' is not read. For empty, not-found, no-results, offline and stale, role and aria-live become undefined in the same render that swaps the text, so the region is no longer live when the outcome arrives and nothing is announced. The test at feedback-state.test.tsx:23-32 checks that this pattern is present. It does not check that anything gets announced. The title at :189-191 is a plain div, while EmptyTitle is role=heading aria-level=3 (empty.tsx:53-58). The non-heading title is minor; the missing announcements are a real K2 gap.

findings.subject: load-more-trigger
findings.summary: The Retry action is a bare text button about 15px tall with no coarse-pointer target expansion.
findings.evidence: load-more-trigger.css:88-96 (padding: 0; border: 0; inline text); glyphs span y 36-51 in apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-loadmoretrigger-failed-chromium-linux.png; no --a63-control-min-target rule. findings.fix: Render Retry with the DS Button (size sm, ghost or link variant), which carries min-target handling and hover/active states, or add a ::after hit area sized to --a63-control-min-target.

verified.reason: load-more-trigger.css:88-96 gives .a63-LoadMoreTrigger-action padding 0, border 0 and inline text, with no min-height/min-width and no --a63-control-min-target. grep finds no coarse-pointer rule in that file. findings.subject: chat-typing-indicator
findings.summary: ChatTypingIndicator's announcement is unreliable and suppressed in its documented usage, and its dots vanish under forced colors.
findings.evidence: chat-typing-indicator.tsx:22-28 mounts role=status with only aria-label and no text, so there is no content change to announce; every documented placement nests it in ChatMessage streaming, which sets aria-busy=true (chat-message.tsx:69; chat-typing-indicator.stories.tsx:22-24; packages/templates/src/blocks/chat-panel/chat-panel.tsx:131-146; apps/docs/src/pages/pattern-agent.mdx:67-82); dots are background-color: currentColor only (chat-typing-indicator.css:22) with no forced-colors rule (grep forced-colors in components/chat-*: none).
findings.fix: Render the label as visually hidden text inside the status (not aria-label), and document or enforce that the status sits outside any aria-busy ancestor (or have ChatMessage not set aria-busy while it holds only the indicator). Add @media (forced-colors: active) { .a63-ChatTypingIndicator-dot { background-color: CanvasText; forced-color-adjust: none } } or draw the dots with a border. Add a test for the in-message placement.

verified.reason: Reproduced from source. chat-typing-indicator.tsx:22-37 renders role=status whose only children are aria-hidden dots, so the live region has no text content; its name comes only from aria-label. A live region that mounts already filled, with nothing changing inside it afterwards, is not reliably announced, so the comment at lines 12-14 ('announces it once') overstates what happens. Every documented usage nests it in ChatMessage with streaming: chat-message.tsx:69 sets aria-busy={streaming}. The InMessage story (stories.tsx:22-24), ChatPanel's assistant message (chat-panel.tsx:131 sets streaming, the indicator is at :145-146) and the docs pattern (pattern-agent.mdx ~66-80, getMessageText(message) || <ChatTypingIndicator/> inside ChatMessage streaming) all do this. aria-busy on an ancestor lets assistive technology hold back changes until the busy state ends, which makes the announcement even less likely. Forced colors: chat-typing-indicator.css:22 paints the dots with background-color: currentColor. Forced-colors mode replaces background-color with Canvas, the dots have no border or outline, and grep finds no forced-colors rule in components/chat-*. In that mode the component's only visible content disappears. Both are K2 gaps: wrong role/name behaviour and forced colors. The 'ready' blocker is the vanishing dots, so P1 stands rather than P0, because the message still arrives as text afterwards.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx VideoBlock
findings.summary: VideoBlock can play an endless looping video with no pause control, and autoplay ignores prefers-reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: packages/mdx/src/blocks/video-block/video-block.tsx:57-88 passes autoPlay/loop/controls straight to <video>; stories AutoplayLoop (video-block.stories.tsx:50-57) and DecorativeBackground (:59-71) ship autoPlay+loop+controls={false}; grep 'reduce' in video-block -> none. Fails WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide, level A).
findings.fix: Under useMdxReducedMotion() do not autoplay; whenever autoPlay is set and controls is false, render a labelled pause/play toggle over the video; add a test for both, and drop aria-label on captionPolicy='decorative' (aria-hidden instead).

verified.reason: Reproduced from source. video-block.tsx:56-88 forwards autoPlay, loop and controls straight to <video> with no pause control and no reduced-motion check. Grepping packages/mdx/src for prefers-reduced-motion/useReducedMotion finds only page-table-of-contents and the primitives/use-reduced-motion.ts helper, and VideoBlock does not use either. The AutoplayLoop and DecorativeBackground stories (video-block.stories.tsx:50-71) ship autoPlay+loop+controls={false}, so the package itself demonstrates an endless loop that cannot be paused. This fails WCAG 2.2.2 and the K2 reduced-motion requirement. Defaults (autoPlay=false, controls=true) are safe, so the failure needs opt-in props, but those props are documented and shown in stories.

findings.subject: @atom63/widgets WidgetStateFeedback, WidgetAvatar, WidgetHostedShell (widget controls)
findings.summary: Widget controls are pinned to 24px on coarse pointers; the promised 44px hit area via --widget-interaction-target is never applied.
findings.evidence: packages/widgets/src/layout/widget-scale.ts:64-96 sets --a63-control-min-target to 24px and says 44px comes from --widget-interaction-target (:73-84), set at :159; `grep -rn widget-interaction-target` over the repo finds only widget-scale.ts and widget-scale.test.ts:105-122 (which asserts the variable's value, not a rendered hit box). Retry/details buttons (state/widget-state-feedback.tsx:47-70), avatar shuffle and host error retry are therefore 24px on phones.
findings.fix: Consume the variable: in widget CSS, under @media (pointer: coarse), give widget buttons an ::after hit expansion of max(100%, var(--widget-interaction-target)) centred on the control; add a browser test that measures the hit box at 44 physical px.

verified.reason: Reproduced. widget-scale.ts controlTargetStyle pins --a63-control-min-target, -lg and -xl to 24px; the comment at :73-84 promises 44px through --widget-interaction-target, which is set only at :159 (and only in widgetPresentationStyle; widgetUnitStyle never sets it). Outside widget-scale.ts, the test and the api.md type, no CSS anywhere reads the variable. The Button hit area is button.css:131-138 ::before { min-width/min-height: var(--a63-control-min-target) }, so inside a widget the hit area also resolves to 24px. Coarse-pointer targets are therefore 24px, against the K5 44px rule. This meets WCAG 2.5.8 AA but not the repo's own bar.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx blocks (26 of 30: all except Callout, KeyIdea, ExampleContainer and the prose map)
findings.summary: Most MDX blocks have no usable docs: one row in an intent table, no props, no example, no playground, and the CLI answers with an import line only.

findings.subject: shadcn reverse bridge (compat/a63-from-shadcn.css)
findings.summary: The reverse shadcn bridge leaves 139 tokens that ui-react recipes read without a fallback undefined, so a shadcn host following the README gets collapsed spacing, invisible selected states and missing type/disabled styling.
findings.evidence: Scripted measurement over the 72 files imported by packages/ui-react/src/styles/recipes.css: 234 --a63-* reads without fallback, 21 declared in recipes, 107 declared in compat/a63-from-shadcn.css, 139 missing (e.g. --a63-space-0_5 x16 files, --a63-space-1_5 x7, --a63-text-accent x8, --a63-selected-background/-foreground, --a63-selected-accent-*, --a63-action-disabled-*, --a63-type-display-*, --a63-font-app, --a63-category-*). README: packages/styles/README.md shadcn table; consumer: packages/mdx/src/styles/shadcn.css:11. Only test: recipes.test.ts:78-81 (four strings).
findings.fix: Either import the contracts and the non-color foundation (space, type, motion, radius) from the reverse entry and define the remaining color roles from shadcn names, or generate a63-from-shadcn.css from the manifest; add a test that every no-fallback --a63-* read in recipes.css resolves when only a63-from-shadcn + recipes.css are loaded.

verified.reason: I reproduced the measurement with a script over the 71 files that recipes.css @imports. It found 234 --a63-* reads with no fallback; 139 are declared neither in the recipes nor in compat/a63-from-shadcn.css. Missing examples: --a63-space-0_5 (16 files), --a63-space-1_5 (7), --a63-text-accent (8), --a63-selected-background/-foreground (3), --a63-selected-accent-* (4), plus control-feedback-ease/duration (40/39) and control-icon-size-*. The bridge (158 lines) has no @import to supply them. It is an exported entry (styles/package.json:33), documented for external shadcn hosts (README.md:194,227), and consumed by mdx/src/styles/shadcn.css:11. Because the tokens are undefined, padding collapses to 0, selected washes become transparent and icon sizes fall back to defaults, which is a documented path that is broken in practice. Some of the misses (overlay gloss/texture) degrade harmlessly to none, but the spacing and selected-state misses are enough to block 'ready'.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx
findings.summary: @atom63/mdx labels 13 of 14 entries 'stable' (a major-version compatibility promise) while it is 0.4.0-beta.3, stable promotion is not approved, and it has broken exports in a patch before; 20 of its public types cannot be imported by name.

'stable'); packages/mdx/README.md:17-26; tierDefinitions.stable 'breaking changes need a major version'; docs/design-system/audits/stable-release-preflight.json stablePromotionApproved:false; packages/mdx/CHANGELOG.md:105 (0.3.2 removed mdxTypography.docsBody/docsLead/docsListItem); ae-forgotten-export in packages/mdx/api/mdx.api.md (MdxComponentsMap, ComparisonContextValue, MdxParagraph, MdxCode, MdxAnchor, MdxImage), mdx.blocks.api.md (CompareItem, StepsStep, TimelineItem, ScrollStageStep, VideoCaptionPolicy, CodeBlockVariant, MediaSpacing, TableOfContentsVariant, MdxPageSkeletonVariant, aspectRatioClasses, fitClasses), mdx.primitives.api.md (MdxFrameHeading, spacingClasses).

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx, @atom63/inform, @atom63/widgets
findings.summary: mdx, inform and widgets take @atom63/ui-react as a regular dependency pinned to an exact version, so a consumer whose ui-react differs gets a second ui-react copy (split theme/UIProvider contexts, duplicate CSS); with the stale latest tags the documented untagged installs already mix versions.

findings.subject: slider

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: The unfilled rail is nearly invisible in every theme and mode (1.02-1.18:1 against the page), so the range extent and the remaining amount cannot be seen.

Track = --a63-surface-muted (slider.css:38). Progress, using a border + field background (progress.css:29-31), stays visible.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: Slider's default tone is accent, while AGENTS.md rule 5 says to set tone="accent" on a Slider only when it is one of the view's one or two accent cues.

findings.fix: Either make `neutral` the contract default for Slider and Progress (matching SegmentedControl, whose default is neutral), or reword rule 5; regenerate contracts and baselines.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: In light mode the stars fail 3:1 non-text contrast: on stars 2.04:1 and off stars 1.64:1 against the page.
findings.evidence: Measured on ui-react-rating-themes-chromium-linux.png row 1: on rgb(243,159,0), off rgb(197,197,197), page rgb(249,249,249). --rating-on = --a63-category-amber (= --color-warning-500), --rating-off = text-secondary at 35% (rating.css:11-12).
findings.fix: Use a darker amber step (or the -subtle-foreground) for --rating-on in light mode and raise --rating-off, or outline off stars, so on/off reach 3:1 against the surface.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: The input rating is controlled-only (value required, no defaultValue), and the radio rounds the value while the star fill does not.
findings.evidence: rating.tsx:10-23 (value: number required); rating.tsx:85 String(Math.round(value)) vs rating.tsx:92 data-on={star <= value}: value=2.5 checks radio 3 while only 2 stars are on.
findings.fix: Add defaultValue with internal state (useControlled-style), and derive data-on from the same rounded value used for the radio.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: Rating looks identical in all four themes, and its Themes story has no row labels and uneven rows.
findings.evidence: ui-react-rating-themes-chromium-linux.png: same amber lucide stars in all 8 rows, no theme/mode labels (other batch stories label rows), retro/light row taller than the others.
findings.fix: Decide whether rating expresses the theme archetype (e.g. retro bevel or terminal glyph) or stays a neutral content colour; at minimum label the Themes rows like checkbox/slider and even the row heights.

findings.subject: progress

findings.subject: spinner

findings.subject: spinner

findings.subject: spinner

findings.subject: feedback-state

verified.reason: Real: FeedbackStateProps (feedback-state.tsx:49-60) is a closed interface, the destructure at :155-166 has no rest, and the root div at :173-181 takes no spread props and no ref. K1's hard requirements, however, are 'props match the contract' and 'composition spreads props/forwards refs'. The generated contract (feedback-state-contract.ts) defines only kinds, sizes, slots and states, all of which are honoured, and FeedbackState is not an asChild/render part. Consumers can still wrap it to add id or aria. This matches the bar's P2 wording ('works, with a known gap a consumer can hit'), not a ready-blocker.

findings.subject: ReaderLayout
findings.summary: Nothing leads a builder to ReaderLayout: `atom63 build` for a docs or article idea never names it (it suggests compact density and list-page), there is no example, and the docs mention it in one snippet.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 build "a docs article page with a table of contents"` -> Compact density, list-page, chat-page, dashboard-page, data-table-section; Foundation lists Page, Container, Section, SectionHeader only. `atom63 build "a blog post reading layout"` -> app-view. `atom63 example reader-layout` -> component.not_found. apps/docs/src/pages/pattern-layout.mdx:51 is the only mention.
findings.fix: Add ReaderLayout to the build kit's Foundation list and to the reading/docs/article intent; document its props (aside, reserveAside) and when to use it on pattern-layout; make its story reachable by `atom63 example`. Also stop 'table of contents' from triggering compact density.

verified.reason: The gap is real but the finding overstates it. `atom63 build "a docs article page with a table of contents"` does return compact density, list-page, chat-page, dashboard-page, data-table-section and no ReaderLayout. `atom63 search article` and `atom63 search docs` do not surface it either, and `atom63 example reader-layout` gives component.not_found. But 'nothing leads a builder to it' is wrong: `atom63 search reader` returns `api ReaderLayout`, `atom63 api ReaderLayout` prints the import and points to `atom63 docs pattern-layout`, and apps/docs/src/components/docs-page.tsx uses it. ReaderLayout is a layout primitive, not a template, so `copy` does not apply, and a builder can still put together a reading column from Container/Section. It is a gap a builder can hit (P2), not a blocker for 'ready'.

verified.reason: The mechanism is real and I reproduced it from the source. brand-action.css:14-15 redeclares primary on [data-a63-brand]. semantics.css:95-97 and :306 declare --a63-text-accent (161/360), --a63-focus-ring (209/395), --a63-chart-1 (269/416) and --a63-selected-accent-background (301/445) only on :root, .light and [data-a63-mode]. provider.tsx:68 stamps data-a63-brand alone, so under a nested UIProvider brand=... with no mode those tokens inherit values already resolved against the root brand. This contradicts personalization-axes.md 'Declare derived tokens on the scope that changes them'. The severity is inflated, though. The main personalization path stamps the brand on the document root (apply-personalization.ts:48), where everything resolves correctly. Passing mode together with brand also fixes it, because the [data-a63-mode] block then redeclares on the same element. The only in-repo nested usages (button.stories.tsx:692, switch.stories.tsx:327) pass brand together with mode. The defect only hits brand-without-mode nesting, so it does not block 'ready'.

verified.reason: Real, by the same mechanism as r1-tokens-1. surface.css remaps --surface-light-*/--surface-dark-* on [data-a63-surface]. semantics.css consumes them only in the :root,.light,[data-a63-mode] block (95-185) and the dark block (306-379). provider.tsx:73 stamps data-a63-surface alone, and --a63-surface-tint is declared only on :root (semantics.css:14). findings.evidence: segmented-control.tsx:83-93 (Tabs.Tab with aria-label and title = item.label even in the label variant). Screen readers announce 'tab, 1 of 3' with no panel to move to.
findings.fix: Decide whether a mode switch without panels should be a radiogroup or a toggle-group pattern; in any case drop `title` in the label variant (keep it only for icon-only segments).

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: The contract's disabled state has no story or visual baseline, and there is no RTL story.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.json:9 lists 'disabled'; grep 'disabled' in segmented-control.stories.tsx returns nothing; no segmentedcontrol-*disabled* or *right-to-left* baseline in apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/.
findings.fix: Add a States story (disabled segment, accent + neutral) and a RightToLeft story, and regenerate baselines.

findings.subject: segmented-control
findings.summary: Two boolean props (animateBackplate, fullWidth) and an items-array-only API; segments cannot carry custom content.
findings.evidence: segmented-control.tsx:25-32.
findings.fix: Keep for now; if the API is revisited, express layout as a `width` axis (auto | fill) in the contract and consider composable segment children.

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: The disabled state and a thumb hover state are not designed or captured.
findings.evidence: slider.json:8 lists 'disabled'; no disabled story (grep in slider.stories.tsx); slider.css has no :hover rule for the thumb.
findings.fix: Add a disabled example to a States story and a hover affordance on the thumb (gated by @media (hover: hover)).

findings.subject: slider
findings.summary: The neutral tone fills with --a63-text-primary as a background (a craft-baseline token-role entry), and Progress does the same through a custom property that the check does not see.
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json:10 ('token-role | slider.css | background-color: var(--a63-text-primary)'); slider.css:49-51; progress.css:50-52 (--progress-fill: var(--a63-text-primary)).
findings.fix: Introduce or reuse a neutral solid token (e.g. --a63-action-neutral as Toggle does) for both fills and remove the baseline entry.

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: The hover preview is not gated by (hover: hover), so a tap leaves a sticky preview on touch devices.
findings.evidence: rating.css:83-88 (:has(.a63-Rating-item:hover) and :hover ~ rules outside any hover media query).
findings.fix: Wrap the two hover rules in @media (hover: hover).

findings.subject: rating
findings.summary: The arrow-key behaviour the contract promises is untested, and an input rating without `label` renders an unnamed radiogroup.
findings.evidence: rating.json:5 ('so arrow keys change the value'); rating.test.tsx has 3 cases, none keyboard; rating.tsx:79 aria-label={label} with label optional.
findings.fix: Add an ArrowRight/ArrowLeft test, and warn in development (or require label/aria-labelledby in types) for the input form.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: The WithLabelAndValue example names the bar 'Example progress' with aria-label, overriding its visible ProgressLabel 'Downloading' (label in name mismatch).
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/progress/progress.stories.tsx:34-36; served verbatim by `pnpm -s atom63 example progress WithLabelAndValue`.
findings.fix: Drop aria-label from the composed example so ProgressLabel names the bar.

findings.subject: progress
findings.summary: The indeterminate sweep uses physical translateX, so it runs left-to-right in right-to-left layouts.
findings.evidence: progress.css:66-73.
findings.fix: Flip the keyframes under :dir(rtl) (e.g. a --progress-dir multiplier as switch.css does).

findings.subject: spinner
findings.summary: The reduced-motion still frame (a static quarter arc) is not captured or tested.
findings.evidence: spinner.json:6 lists 'reduced-motion'; spinner.tsx:20-24; no reduced-motion story or test.
findings.fix: Add a reduced-motion story/baseline and a test asserting animation: none.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: Checkbox and Switch have no forced-colors repaint; their checked state survives only through the icon or thumb position, and neither is in the forced-colors regression list.
findings.evidence: No forced-colors block in checkbox.css or switch.css; recipes.test.ts:368-377 lists radio but not checkbox or switch.
findings.fix: Repaint checked state with Highlight/HighlightText as radio.css:126-136 does, and add both to the recipes.test.ts list.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: The contract's invalid state is styled but never captured in a story or baseline.
findings.evidence: checkbox.json:8 'invalid'; checkbox.css:109-111; checkbox.stories.tsx States (lines 28-38) has no aria-invalid example (radio.stories.tsx:116 does).
findings.fix: Add an invalid checkbox to the States story and regenerate the baseline.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: Checkbox, Radio and Switch always fill with the brand accent and have no tone axis, while AGENTS.md rule 5 says 'Selection is neutral by default'.
findings.evidence: checkbox.css:11, radio.css:17, switch.css:28 (--a63-selection-accent -> --a63-action-primary); checkbox.mdx 'the checked fill is the brand primary'; AGENTS.md rule 5.
findings.fix: Decide whether rule 5's 'selection' excludes these form controls (then say so in the rule) or whether they get a neutral default.

findings.subject: radio
findings.summary: Radio stories teach duplicate option names and unnamed groups.
findings.evidence: radio.stories.tsx:107-116: two radios both named 'Example radio option', groups without aria-label (the conformance test does name its group).
findings.fix: Give each option a distinct name and each RadioGroup an aria-label in the stories.

findings.subject: switch
findings.summary: The switch hover rule is not gated by (hover: hover), unlike checkbox and radio.
findings.evidence: switch.css:137-139 vs checkbox.css:94-98 and radio.css:96-100.
findings.fix: Wrap the hover rule in @media (hover: hover).

findings.subject: switch
findings.summary: The thumb-icon example labels the state ('Dark appearance' / 'Light appearance') instead of the setting, against the component's own guidance.
findings.evidence: switch.stories.tsx:121 aria-label={checked ? 'Dark appearance' : 'Light appearance'}; `atom63 component switch` guidance: 'Label the setting rather than the state'.
findings.fix: Use a fixed label such as 'Dark appearance' and let aria-checked carry the state.

findings.subject: input-otp
findings.summary: Retro OTP draws its bevel on every slot, so the fused pill looks heavier than a retro Input.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-inputotp-themes-chromium-linux.png retro rows
findings.fix: YZ to judge; option: draw the retro bevel on the group, not each slot.

findings.subject: input-otp
findings.summary: Caret uses --a63-text-primary as a background colour (craft-baseline token-role entry).
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json:8; input-otp.css:104-107
findings.fix: Set color: var(--a63-text-primary) and background-color: currentColor, then drop the baseline entry.

findings.subject: select
findings.summary: Runtime craft baseline accepts Select options that take focus with no outline change.
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/runtime-craft-baseline.json:2-11
findings.fix: Background highlight is the APG norm: replace the baseline entries with a commented craft disable on those stories, or add an inset outline on [data-highlighted]:focus-visible.

findings.subject: label
findings.summary: Label text is always control-font-size-md, so it does not follow an sm or lg field.
findings.evidence: label.css:14
findings.fix: Inherit size from a Field/size context or document that Label is size-independent.

findings.subject: amount
findings.summary: `strong` is a weight boolean rather than an axis.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/amount/amount.tsx:16
findings.fix: Acceptable while there are two weights; revisit if a third appears.

findings.subject: input
findings.summary: No field story shows RTL, long or CJK strings.
findings.evidence: grep rtl/dir=/long in batch stories: only amount and select (LONG list)
findings.fix: Add one RTL + CJK long-value frame to Input, Select and Field stories.

findings.subject: dialog
findings.summary: Phone bottom-sheet dialog has square top corners.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/dialog/dialog.css:93; apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-dialog-open-phone-chromium-linux.png.
findings.fix: Keep the top radius on bottom-stuck dialogs (YZ taste).

findings.subject: sheet
findings.summary: Overlay family typography/spacing differs: Sheet title lg + space-6, Dialog/Drawer title xl + space-5; AlertDialog footer and Sheet inset read --radius-2xl, not --a63-overlay-radius.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/sheet/sheet.css:141,176-181,131-133; alert-dialog/alert-dialog.css:160-161.
findings.fix: Pick one overlay header scale and read --a63-overlay-radius everywhere.

findings.subject: tooltip
findings.summary: Tooltip, Drawer and Sheet sides are physical only (baseline debt).
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/contract-consistency-baseline.json:2-9.
findings.fix: Add inline-start/inline-end to tooltip sides; YZ decides whether Drawer/Sheet get start/end.

findings.subject: alert-dialog
findings.summary: AlertDialog variants mix action tone (destructive) with status (info/success/warning); sizes use default where the system says md (baseline debt, also Dialog).
findings.evidence: contract-consistency-baseline.json:10-11,17.
findings.fix: Resolve with the contract-consistency cleanup.

findings.subject: drawer
findings.summary: Drawer grab handle is barely visible.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-drawer-persistent-sheet-chromium-linux.png; drawer.css:200.
findings.fix: Use a stronger token (e.g. --a63-border-strong) for the handle.

findings.subject: popover
findings.summary: Popover and HoverCard do not wrap long unbroken strings.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/popover/popover.css:17-40, hover-card.css:21-48 (no overflow-wrap) vs tooltip.css:91.
findings.fix: Add overflow-wrap:anywhere.

findings.subject: dialog
findings.summary: No long-string, CJK or RTL story for Dialog/AlertDialog.
findings.evidence: dialog.stories.tsx and alert-dialog.stories.tsx exports.
findings.fix: Add a stress story.

findings.subject: command
findings.summary: Command nests a bordered panel inside a bordered popup; in retro it reads as a double frame.
findings.evidence: command.css:53 (popup border) and :130-138 (panel border + shadow); ui-react-command-themes-chromium-linux.png retro light/dark; AGENTS.md rule 7.
findings.fix: YZ to confirm on the contact sheet; if kept, drop the panel border where the theme already draws a panel shadow.

findings.subject: breadcrumb
findings.summary: In terminal, the current page takes the accent colour while links are navy, so the non-link looks like the most clickable item.
findings.evidence: ui-react-breadcrumb-themes-chromium-linux.png terminal light/dark rows ('Atom63' in accent).
findings.fix: YZ to confirm; otherwise give .a63-Breadcrumb-page text-primary in terminal like other themes.

findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: The static menu gallery draws the radio item with a Circle icon, but the shipped RadioItem renders a check, so the baseline does not show the real radio state.
findings.evidence: menu.stories.tsx:56 (Circle) vs dropdown-menu.tsx:192-194 and menubar.tsx:172-175 (check icon).
findings.fix: Use the same check indicator in the gallery (or change RadioItem to a dot if that is the intent).

findings.subject: dropdown-menu
findings.summary: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem and RadioItem lack the `inset` prop that MenubarCheckboxItem and MenubarRadioItem have.
findings.evidence: dropdown-menu.tsx:158-200 vs menubar.tsx:126-180.
findings.fix: Add `inset` to the DropdownMenu and ContextMenu checkbox/radio items for parity.

findings.subject: menubar
findings.summary: The menubar recipe header points at a nonexistent a63-DropdownMenu-* recipe.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menubar/menubar.css:6-8 (the shared recipe is a63-Menu-* in menu/menu.css).
findings.fix: Correct the comment to the a63-Menu-* recipe.

findings.subject: card
findings.summary: The card cursor label uses text-primary as a fill and surface-page as text (a role inversion; both are craft-baseline entries).
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json token-role entries for card.css; card.css:417-418.
findings.fix: Use an inverse-surface pair (or the tooltip tokens) for the pill and drop the baseline entries.

findings.subject: frame
findings.summary: Frame border names overstate their weights: subtle is 20% of border-subtle (near invisible) and strong is plain border-subtle.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/frame/frame.css:85-93.
findings.fix: YZ to confirm the intended weights; possibly map strong to border-control.

findings.subject: frame
findings.summary: Frame parts take no render prop, so FrameTitle cannot become a heading.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/frame/frame.tsx:115-122.
findings.fix: Use useRender on FrameTitle (and the other parts), as Card does.

findings.subject: resizable
findings.summary: Resizable takes two props for one axis (direction and orientation) and a deprecated withHandle boolean.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/resizable/resizable.tsx:18-19,36,62-63.
findings.fix: Deprecate direction and type orientation from the contract.

findings.subject: scrollable-list
findings.summary: The scrollable-list end chevron covers the last visible item, with little visible fade.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-scrollablelist-themes-chromium-linux.png.
findings.fix: YZ to judge; possibly add inline-end padding under the control or a stronger mask.

findings.subject: item
findings.summary: Item sub-parts have no render prop, and the item contract keeps the default / focus synonyms.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/item/item.tsx:110-167; contract-consistency-baseline.json item.sizes default->md, item.states focus->focus-visible.
findings.fix: Align with the contract-consistency decision (layer 2).

findings.subject: sidebar
findings.summary: Menu button sizes use "default" while sub-button sizes use "md" in the same component.
findings.evidence: sidebar.json menuButtonSizes ["default","sm","lg"] vs menuSubButtonSizes ["sm","md"]; the contract-consistency lint does not see it (only table.sizes is baselined).
findings.fix: Rename menu button "default" to "md" with a deprecated alias, and extend the lint to every *Sizes list.

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
findings.summary: The disclosure chevron snaps instead of rotating.
findings.evidence: sidebar-nav-tree.css:192 transitions transform, but rotation uses the rotate property (css:37,195).
findings.fix: Transition rotate instead of transform.

findings.subject: sidebar-nav-tree
findings.summary: Long labels cannot be revealed on touch.
findings.evidence: Ticker reveal is hover/focus only (text-ticker.css:26-29); nav rows are touch targets with no long-press reveal.
findings.fix: Allow labels to wrap to two lines on coarse pointers, or reveal on the active row.

findings.subject: app-view
findings.summary: topBarSpan="main" renders two elements with data-slot="app-view-body".
findings.evidence: app-view.tsx:150 and :166.
findings.fix: Give the inner wrapper its own slot name (e.g. app-view-content-body) and add it to the contract.

findings.subject: app-view
findings.summary: The component PhoneWith* baselines are taken at desktop width.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-appview-phone-with-tab-bar-chromium-linux.png and the other PhoneWith* PNGs are 1280x900; only the templates baselines are at phone width.
findings.fix: Rename the stories with the Phone suffix the visual runner uses for a 390px viewport (as DarkSidebarPhone does), and regenerate.

findings.subject: table
findings.summary: Numeric columns have no end-aligned, tabular-figure affordance.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-table-themes-chromium-linux.png shows the Amount column start-aligned; table.css has no numeric cell rule.
findings.fix: Add a numeric cell option (data-align="end" + tabular-nums) and use it in the stories.

findings.subject: carousel
findings.summary: In light modes the slide has no surface, while dark modes draw a card.
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-carousel-themes-chromium-linux.png: modern/retro/terminal light show no slide boundary; all dark cells show a card.
findings.fix: YZ to decide whether the slide surface should read the same in both modes.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: badge.mdx and the badge contract description name tokens the recipe no longer reads.
findings.evidence: badge.mdx 'backed by the foundation --color-* tokens' and token list --a63-status-info; badge.css reads --a63-category-*-subtle and --a63-status-*-subtle; badge.json description cites the --a63-badge-* contract.
findings.fix: Update the mdx and contract description to the category/status-subtle tokens.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Interactive Badge has no active state, and focus-visible is not captured in a baseline.
findings.evidence: badge.css interactive block has hover only; apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-badge-interactive-chromium-linux.png shows rest and disabled.
findings.fix: Add an active treatment and a focus-visible capture.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Badge heights are fixed rem and do not follow compact density.
findings.evidence: badge.css:10, sizes block: 1rem / 1.25rem / 1.5rem.
findings.fix: Derive heights from --a63-space-unit or control size tokens.

findings.subject: skeleton
findings.summary: Skeleton disappears in forced-colors mode.
findings.evidence: skeleton.css:7-12 background-color only; no @media (forced-colors: active) rule.
findings.fix: Add a forced-colors rule (for example a CanvasText 1px outline or GrayText background with forced-color-adjust: none).

findings.subject: animated-check
findings.summary: AnimatedCheck's draw duration is a raw 300ms, not a motion token.
findings.evidence: animated-check.tsx:17 animation: a63-animated-check-draw 300ms ease-out forwards.
findings.fix: Use a --a63-motion-* duration and easing token.

findings.subject: empty
findings.summary: The expanded error detail has no visual baseline.
findings.evidence: Baselines: ui-react-empty-error-state shows collapsed only.
findings.fix: Add an expanded ErrorState story.

findings.subject: alert
findings.summary: Component guidance is generic boilerplate across the batch.
findings.evidence: `pnpm -s atom63 component alert` guidance bullets 2-3 ('Keep product data and fetching outside...', 'Test long, empty, and narrow content...') repeat verbatim for badge and others.
findings.fix: Write component-specific guidance (when to use Alert vs Toaster vs FeedbackState, role choice).

findings.subject: chat-composer
findings.summary: Inline-to-block switching only re-measures on typing, so a host-set value or a resize leaves the layout stale.
findings.evidence: chat-composer.tsx:139-143 and 178-185: wrappedAt is set only inside onChange via wraps().
findings.fix: Measure in a layout effect keyed on value and on a ResizeObserver of the field.

findings.subject: chat-composer
findings.summary: The focus-visible state the contract lists has no baseline.
findings.evidence: chat-composer.json states include focus-visible; no ui-react-chatcomposer-*focus* screenshot exists in apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__.
findings.fix: Add a focused story (play focuses the field) and baseline.

findings.subject: chat-composer
findings.summary: Generated guidance bullets are generic boilerplate that does not fit the chat components.
findings.evidence: `atom63 component chat-composer` bullets 2-3 mention errors and an invalid state the composer does not have; chat-typing-indicator bullet 2 talks about a 'utility'; chat-message, chat-steps and message repeat 'Keep product data and fetching outside...'.
findings.fix: Replace the archetype boilerplate with component-specific guidance in apps/docs/src/lib/component-catalog.ts.

findings.subject: chat-steps
findings.summary: Long step titles are not broken, unlike descriptions.
findings.evidence: chat-steps.css:117-120 sets overflow-wrap:anywhere on the description only; .a63-ChatStep-title has none.
findings.fix: Apply overflow-wrap:anywhere to .a63-ChatStep-body.

findings.subject: chat-steps
findings.summary: Status-label translation API differs between ChatStep (per-item statusLabel) and Message (statusLabels map).
findings.evidence: chat-steps.tsx:66 vs message.tsx:62.
findings.fix: Accept a statusLabels map on ChatSteps (or ChatStep) to match Message.

findings.subject: chat-steps
findings.summary: ChatSteps barely changes across modern, aqua and retro, and the connector hairline is nearly invisible.
findings.evidence: ui-react-chatsteps-themes-chromium-linux.png.
findings.fix: YZ to judge whether the archetype needs per-theme expression and a stronger connector.

findings.subject: message
findings.summary: Message has no RTL story or baseline, and no chat component has a CJK long-string story.
findings.evidence: message.stories.tsx exports Playground, Thread, DeliveryStates, Media, LongContent, Themes only; no CJK strings in any chat story.
findings.fix: Add a RightToLeft Message story and a CJK long-text case to the chat stories.

findings.subject: message
findings.summary: status renders on incoming messages and avatar is silently dropped on outgoing.
findings.evidence: message.tsx:59 docs say outgoing only, but tsx:109-122 renders it for any direction; tsx:95 ignores avatar when outgoing.
findings.fix: Document both, or ignore status on incoming consistently with avatar.

findings.subject: chat-message
findings.summary: None of chat-message, chat-steps or chat-typing-indicator has its own phone story; phone width is seen only through templates.
findings.evidence: Story exports listed by `atom63 component <slug>`; templates-blocks-chat-panel-phone-chromium-linux.png is the only phone capture.
findings.fix: Add a phone-width story per component or a shared chat phone story.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx CodeBlock
findings.summary: CodeBlock branches on dark mode for Shiki colours (known craft debt).
findings.evidence: packages/mdx/src/blocks/code-block/code-block.tsx:81,135 'dark:[&_.shiki]:text-[var(--shiki-dark)]'; docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json:2-3.
findings.fix: Set one --code-token-color custom property in code-block.css that resolves from the mode token, so the component class has no dark: branch.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx Timeline
findings.summary: Timeline's dot uses a text token as a fill (known token-role debt).
findings.evidence: docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json:5 'token-role | packages/mdx/src/blocks/timeline/timeline.css | background-color: var(--a63-text-primary)'.
findings.fix: Use an indicator or border-strong token for the marker fill.

findings.subject: @atom63/inform InformSpotlight
findings.summary: The spotlight Phone story renders a stray second 'Target control' button, visible dimmed in the baseline.
findings.evidence: packages/inform/src/surfaces/inform-spotlight.stories.tsx:17-33 (meta decorator) plus :66-77 (story decorator); apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/inform-spotlight-phone-chromium-linux.png.
findings.fix: Give Phone its own render instead of stacking a second decorator.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx blocks, @atom63/inform, @atom63/widgets
findings.summary: Axis types used in public props are not exported (CalloutType, CodeBlockVariant, MdxPageSkeletonVariant, InformAction from /surfaces and others).
findings.evidence: packages/mdx/api/mdx.blocks.api.md:44-657 (14 ae-forgotten-export), inform.surfaces.api.md:134-135, inform.react.api.md:47-52, widgets.*.api.md.
findings.fix: Export the prop and axis types from the entry points that use them.

findings.subject: @atom63/brand AppLogo
findings.summary: The horizontal lockup mirrors in RTL, putting the symbol after the wordmark.
findings.evidence: packages/brand/src/logo/app-logo.tsx:88-92 inline-flex row without direction.
findings.fix: Set direction: ltr on the lockup wrapper.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx PageMeta, LayerStack
findings.summary: PageMeta always renders an h1 and LayerStack rows an h3, whatever the page outline.
findings.evidence: page-meta.tsx:39; layer-stack.tsx:55.
findings.fix: Accept a heading level (or as) prop.

findings.subject: @atom63/mdx VideoBlock
findings.summary: VideoBlock hard-codes the source type to video/mp4.
findings.evidence: packages/mdx/src/blocks/video-block/video-block.tsx:92.
findings.fix: Infer the type from the extension or accept a type prop.

findings.subject: Section
findings.summary: Section spacing presets are not monotonic and the top padding is removed by default.
findings.evidence: section.tsx:29-35 gap: loose space-y-8 but generous space-y-6; :18 removeTopSpacing = true.
findings.fix: Make gaps rise with the preset; keep or reconsider the removeTopSpacing default (documented in pattern-layout).

findings.subject: block: detail-panel
findings.summary: The detail sheet opens on the physical right, which is the start side in RTL.
findings.evidence: detail-panel.tsx:49 side="right"; sheet.css:45-48 keeps left/right physical in RTL.
findings.fix: Add an inline-end side to Sheet or pick the side from the direction in the block.

findings.subject: AppView / block: tab-bar
findings.summary: In inset chrome the tab bar's negative margins cancel the root's inline safe-area padding as well as the space-2 gutter.
findings.evidence: app-view.css:181-184 margin-inline: calc(-1 * max(space-2, inset-inline)); tab-bar.tsx:46-47 adds no inline padding.
findings.fix: Pad the tab bar's inline edges with the inline inset after the negative margin.

findings.subject: page: sign-in-page / Page
findings.summary: Bare Page (sign-in) owns no safe-area inset; it works only because the card is narrow and centered.
findings.evidence: sign-in-page.tsx:76 `<Page className="flex items-center px-4">`; page.tsx:16 pads pt-8 pb-20 only.
findings.fix: Pad Page's inline and block edges with max(gutter, --a63-safe-area-*) when it is the outermost frame, or document that the route owns them.

findings.subject: page: onboarding-page
findings.summary: The same 'Create your first invoice' action appears twice on the first-run page (empty-state primary and the current checklist step).
findings.evidence: apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/templates-pages-onboarding-page-desktop-chromium-linux.png.
findings.fix: YZ to decide whether the checklist's current step repeats the action or only points to it.

findings.subject: Semantic color layer and modes (tokens/semantics.css, brand-action.css)
findings.summary: Danger and neutral button labels are tested at 3:1 though they are normal-size text.
findings.evidence: contrast.browser.test.ts:30-33 (primary at 4.5:1 with the comment that labels are text; neutral and danger at AA_UI 3:1). Today white on danger-600 is 6.34:1, so this is a guard gap.
findings.fix: Raise both pairs to 4.5:1.
